THE FULL SPACE VALUE CHAIN

Really interesting seeing how differently major space companies are positioned across launch, manufacturing, spectrum & services heading into 2028:

• $RKLB combines rockets, satellite manufacturing & defense with Iridium global spectrum and 2.55M+ existing subs
• $SPCX controls launch, satellite manufacturing & Starlink through its vertically integrated network
• $ASTS connects everyday smartphones directly to satellites using large arrays & carrier spectrum
• $PL operates Earth observation satellites & sells imagery, data & analytics
• $FLY builds launch vehicles, lunar landers & defense systems
• $YORK manufactures satellites for Pentagon constellations & defense programs
• $RDW supplies spacecraft components, sensors & mission hardware
• $BKSY operates imaging satellites & delivers real time geospatial intelligence

You can also see below how the bigger opportunity in space is shifting toward owning scarce spectrum, infrastructure and recurring customer relationships.

Here's what I found, and thanks again for the correction:

"It's almost always credited to Charles Darwin, but he never wrote or said it. The line comes from Leon C. Megginson, a professor of management and marketing at Louisiana State University, who was paraphrasing Darwin.

The original 1963 wording
Megginson's version appeared in "Lessons from Europe for American Business," published in the Southwestern Social Science Quarterly in 1963 (vol. 44, no. 1, p. 4):

"According to Darwin's Origin of Species, it is not the most intellectual of the species that survives; it is not the strongest that survives; but the species that survives is the one that is able best to adapt and adjust to the changing environment in which it finds itself."

He made a similar statement again in 1964 in Petroleum Management."
~From @perplexity_ai

BREAKING: US imports of semiconductors surged +$2.4 billion in August, to a record $15.4 billion.

This marks their largest monthly increase on record.

Over the last 5 months, US imports of semiconductors have risen +$6.3 billion, or +69%.

YoY, this figure soared +$10.0 billion, or +185%, its largest annual increase in history.

By comparison, during the recovery from the 2008 Financial Crisis, the biggest YoY increase was +69% in January 2011, or +$1.4 billion.

US semiconductor demand is exploding.

posts.name: Steve Burns
posts.text:
Trading is hard here are 10 rules that make it easier:

1. Only trade setups you understand.

2. Know your exit before your entry.

3. Position size small enough to think clearly.

4. Never turn a short-term trade into a long-term investment.

5. Don’t chase trends that are already over extended.

6. Let a price signal confirm your entry.

7. Take the loss when the setup fails and the stop loss is triggered.

8. Stay out when your edge isn’t there.

9. Judge the quality of decisions, not individual trade outcomes.

10. Quantify all your trading rules before your emotions and ego get engaged.

RE: "The 600-1,000 bps deficit jumps in 2009 and 2020 came mostly from discretionary stimulus (ARRA, CARES)."

This was also true in the 2001 recession & the 1991 recession - deficit rose 600 bps of GDP, peak to trough.

And the reason for the "discretionary stimulus" in 2009 & esp. 2020 was to prevent systemic collapse of the system (& UST markets), because they needed to push growth back above rates or face a debt death spiral, or the UST market would have collapsed.  

Druckenmiller gave an interview about this on CNBC in 2021 👇
